description.value:
An elegant two-handed sword. Normal attacks fill a Spirit Gauge; named Spirit techniques replace one of your attacks from the Attack action and spend that gauge. Each technique works on its own — with Extra Attack you can chain two in the same action if you pay both costs.

Open Longsword in the Toolbox

Features

Mastery (Sap)

If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

Spirit Gauge

This weapon holds up to 6 spirit (the gauge starts empty). When you hit a creature with a normal attack using this weapon (an attack you did not replace with a Spirit technique), you gain 1 spirit. You lose all spirit if you don't hit a creature with this weapon within 1 minute or if you become Incapacitated.

Spirit techniques that replace an attack do not generate spirit unless a later upgrade says otherwise. You cannot apply Spirit Blade to the same attack you replace with a Spirit technique.

▸ Upgrade — Spirit Gauge Upgrade II

When you hit with a normal attack using this weapon, you gain 2 spirit instead of 1.

Spirit Blade

When you hit with a normal attack using this weapon, you can expend any number of spirits: the attack deals an extra [[/r 1d4]] slashing damage per spirit expended. You cannot use Spirit Blade on an attack you replaced with Spirit Thrust, Spirit Roundslash, or Spirit Helm Breaker.

▸ Upgrade — Spirit Blade Upgrade I

Spirit Blade extra damage increases to [[/r 1d6]] slashing per spirit expended.

Foresight Slash

Reaction.

As a Reaction when a creature you can see hits you with a melee attack, you can expend 2 spirits. Roll [[/r 1d8]] and add it to your AC against that attack, potentially causing it to miss. If this causes the attack to miss, you can make one attack with this weapon against the attacker as part of the same Reaction, and you regain 1 spirit. You can't use this feature if you have no spirit.

▸ Upgrade — Foresight Slash Upgrade I

When the Foresight Slash counter-attack hits, you gain 1 spirit (in addition to the spirit you regain if you caused the triggering attack to miss).

Spirit Thrust

When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of those attacks with a Spirit Thrust. Expend 2 spirits: this attack deals piercing damage instead of slashing. On a hit, you can move up to 15 feet in a straight line through the target's space without provoking Opportunity Attacks. This attack does not generate spirit.

▸ Upgrade — Spirit Thrust Upgrade I

On a hit, this attack now generates 1 spirit.

Spirit Roundslash

Once per turn when you take the Attack action, you can replace one of those attacks with a Spirit Roundslash. Expend 3 spirits and make an attack against a creature. If another creature is within 5 feet of that target and within your reach, it also takes the weapon's damage, but don't add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. This attack does not generate spirit.

▸ Upgrade — Spirit Roundslash Upgrade I

On a hit, this attack now generates 1 spirit.

Spirit Helm Breaker

Once per turn when you take the Attack action, you can replace one of those attacks with a Spirit Helm Breaker. Expend 3 spirits: you can move up to 10 feet toward the target without provoking Opportunity Attacks, then make the attack. On a hit, the attack deals an extra [[/r 3d6]] slashing damage. If you already resolved another Spirit technique (Spirit Blade, Spirit Thrust, or Spirit Roundslash) during this Attack action, the extra damage is [[/r 4d6]] instead. This attack does not generate spirit. You cannot apply Spirit Blade to this attack.

▸ Upgrade — Spirit Release Slash

Your Helm Breaker improves. If the attack hits and you had 5 or more spirits before the spend, the extra damage is [[/r 5d6]] slashing instead of [[/r 3d6]] (or [[/r 6d6]] instead of [[/r 4d6]] if the combo bonus from another Spirit technique this Attack action also applies).

Special Sheathe (Iai Spirit Slash)

Bonus Action.

As a Bonus Action, you sheathe the blade and enter Iai until the start of your next turn. While in Iai, your Speed is reduced by 10 feet. If a creature hits you or enters your reach while you are in Iai, you can take a Reaction and expend 3 spirits to make an Iai Spirit Slash: one attack with this weapon with Advantage, dealing an extra [[/r 3d6]] slashing damage on a hit. If that attack hits and you had 5 or more spirits before this spend, the target has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn.
